briefing.opening: Good morning, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 23, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Unprecedented Climate Disaster Strikes the World
sections.content: This summer, a deadly heatwave in Europe caused 50,000 deaths, with two-thirds attributed to climate change [1, 44, 46, 58, 60, 61, 70]. Domestically, extreme weather phenomena are intensifying, with heatwaves and heavy rainfall simultaneously rampant in September [6]. Globally, billions of dollars in damage have been caused by hail, and climate change has been shown to exacerbate this [43]. The UK plans to deploy military aircraft to combat wildfires caused by climate change [51], and severe ecosystem changes are being reported due to climate change, including coastal erosion in northern counties and threats to salt lakes [57, 62]. UN experts warn that almost all shallow-water coral reef ecosystems on Earth are at risk of collapse by 2075, urging an urgent response to the unprecedented climate crisis [79].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Domestic Carbon Neutrality Transition and Just Transition Efforts
sections.content: Criteria for 'Just Transition Special Zones' have been established to mitigate employment and local economic impacts from carbon neutrality, with proactive support planned for regions where jobs may decrease [11, 20, 25]. Gwangmyeong City is discussing renewable energy and local energy transition during Climate Week and partnering with businesses to spread a culture of carbon neutrality [23, 33]. Policy efforts continue, such as a National Assembly forum on carbon neutrality held in Yeosu City [14]. At Banwon Elementary School in Seocho-gu, a 'Carbon-Zero Eco Playground' was opened where children learn about carbon neutrality through play [17]. Policies encouraging citizens' green lifestyle practices are also being implemented, such as 4x carbon neutrality points awarded when using G-Bike's shared electric bicycle 'G-Koo' [12, 16]. The Korea Forest Service is promoting the use of domestic timber and strengthening support for wooden architecture and carbon neutrality. Thus, carbon neutrality efforts are materializing in various sectors [13, 15, 18, 19, 22, 24, 26].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Renewable Energy: Crossroads of Opportunity and Challenge
sections.content: In South Korea's utility sector, renewable energy installed capacity has surpassed coal capacity for the first time, signaling a shift in the power landscape [28, 32]. The potential for Korea-Mongolia energy cooperation is being explored through solar facilities next to Mongolian gers [29]. In Gokseong County, efforts to expand renewable energy continue, including the promotion of wind and solar power projects and the establishment of a profit-sharing model for local residents [30, 31, 34, 35, 36, 38]. However, despite the easing of regulations on setback distances for solar power facilities, some local governments are applying old ordinances, causing confusion in permitting [37]. Concerns are also being raised about the issue of uncontrolled solar development, and that while renewable energy installed capacity has surpassed coal, there are still limitations in actual power transmission [39, 40]. Meanwhile, a movement among six New England states in the US to jointly explore nuclear power for energy security, beyond carbon neutrality, illustrates the complex aspects of energy transition [21].

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Action: Policy Discussions and Legal Challenges
sections.content: UN experts emphasize that justice systems on the front lines of the climate crisis must be fit for purpose [52], and there are calls for Congress to seize the opportunity to tackle climate change and lower energy costs [47]. Amid criticism that the climate change agenda has been silent in the midterm elections [54], West Virginia is investigating environmental groups over 'deceptive' climate change advocacy [55, 64, 65, 67]. Climate-related legal disputes continue, such as New York City's attempt to penalize energy companies being dismissed by the courts [59]. In the scientific community, research suggests that climate change has halted the next ice age [45], and efforts are underway to find clues through 'mass extinction' events on whether plants can survive climate change [53, 68]. Furthermore, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly being utilized by climate scientists [82]. While efforts are underway to protect vulnerable households in Grenada from the climate crisis [66], the UK has approved the start of gas production at the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea, continuing the debate on energy transition policies [81].

briefing.closing: In today's briefing, we have examined the severity of global climate disasters, the light and shadow of carbon neutrality efforts and renewable energy transitions both domestically and internationally, and the complex international policy and legal challenges. This is a critical time when comprehensive and consistent efforts are urgently needed to address the climate crisis. This concludes the climate briefing for October 23, 2026.
